Policy: infants born abroad can get a verifiable vaccine record before they obtain civil registration in the host country or a national identity (ID) — and birth registration in the home country still matters.

J1 Issuing digital vaccination certificates (DVCs) for the newborn's birth doses in country A

J1, cross-border birth and initial vaccination. In country A (XXR, the country of birth) the regional hospital gives a newborn who does not hold that country's nationality the two birth doses of hepatitis B vaccine and BCG vaccine, and issues one signed digital vaccination certificate (DVC) per dose (DVCMinPreQual at sub-claim -6) as a paper QR code, without needing a national ID number (and the example in section 12 "QR Code Generation" of the World Health Organization (WHO) guide is a pair of this kind). The hospital's system is the issuer (SMART Trust) and the HCERT side of the verifiable health link (VHL) sharer; the private key stays with the key holder (two-phase signing, <a0>STT-ISS-004</a0>, <a1>STT-COS-006</a1>). The presence of XXR's document signer certificate (DSC), issued under its country signing certificate authority (CSCA), on the GDHCN trust list is a PRECONDITION of issuance, declared below, and not a step. The caregiver is the holder (SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw) and the verifiable health link holder (IHE ITI VHL).
J2 Discovering an unregistered infant and referring them in country B

J2, return home, and discovery and referral by the community health worker (CHW). Back in country B (the home country, XXH), where the family lives, the community health worker, during a home visit, finds an infant born abroad and not listed in the household register. Without a network connection, the community health worker app adds the infant to the household (a Group in FHIR, via a structured data capture form), reads the foreign digital vaccination certificates (DVCs) without verifying them (unverified read, <a0>STT-VER-011</a0>: the triage read stops before the trust-list lookup and marks every field as unverified), saves the doses as reported by the family, not as verified (Immunization.primarySource false), and refers the infant to the clinic for verification. Everything is queued on the phone and synced the next time there is signal. The community health worker app is a receiver (SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw) that deliberately stops before trust verification; the caregiver presents the certificate (VDHC) as the holder (the smart-trust-phw requirement named provide-a-vhl-to-a-receiver).
J3 Verification, import and immunization scheduling at the local clinic

J3, verification at the clinic and generation of the immunization schedule, in country B. The clinic's electronic health record (EHR) (the receiver in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw, and the receiver side of the verifiable health link in IHE ITI VHL) keeps a copy of the GDHCN trust list, which the trust anchor distributes (the trust network anchor; Trust Anchor in IHE) and which country B retrieves as a trust network participant (smart-trust-phw retrieve-pki-material). Loading the DID documents is a PRECONDITION of this visit, not a step in it: the clinic may stay offline the whole time, so the list it verifies against is the last list it refreshed, roughly weekly, when the community health worker (CHW) visits the main clinic or the district health office. The clinic verifies each foreign digital vaccination certificate (DVC) in the <a0>STT-VER-001</a0> order against the DID document of XXR's document signer certificate (DSC), imports the verified doses with their provenance, adds the national immunization schedule code alongside each foreign vaccine code (ConceptMap; the nurse decides on any product without a mapping), and evaluates the national immunization schedule, whereupon the week-6 doses turn out to be due and their appointments are booked.
J4.0 Issuing the family's records to one phone as verifiable health links (VHLs)

J4.0, the family's travel abroad, "one family, one phone". Before travelling, the caregiver who carries the single shared family phone requests from country B's national portal the records of every family member, and chooses for each a passcode the family can say aloud and an expiry date (e.g. 14 days); the portal records this choice as the holder's consent to share (Consent in FHIR, and IHE Privacy Consent on FHIR). The portal, as a verifiable health link sharer (IHE ITI VHL) and issuer (SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw), issues a passcode-protected verifiable health link for each member: the documents (IPS, and DVCs) encrypted as JWE (<a0>STT-VHL-007</a0>) behind an ITI-YY5 manifest, and the link in the SMART Health Links payload format at HCERT key 5 (<a1>STT-VHL-001</a1>, <a2>STT-VHL-002</a2>), signed with country B's document signer certificate (DSC). The shared phone carries the QR codes for the caregiver, who is the verifiable health link (VHL) holder. The records themselves remain hosted in country B: the QR code carries only a pointer and a key.
J4.1 Reading a family member's records at a point of care abroad

J4.1. Abroad, one of the family's children needs care. The caregiver, who is the verifiable health link holder (IHE ITI VHL; and the holder in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw, requirement provide-a-vhl-to-a-receiver), opens her QR code on the family phone and tells the passcode. The hospital system, as a verifiable health link receiver (the receiver in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw), verifies the HCERT against the GDHCN trust list, requests the manifest via ITI-YY5 with an HTTP message signature (<a0>STT-VHL-005</a0>, <a1>STT-VHL-006</a1>, <a2>STT-VHL-008</a2>) and decrypts the documents (<a3>STT-VHL-007</a3>). Country B's portal checks the passcode, returns the manifest and records every request, whether accepted or refused, as an AuditEvent in the home country (IHE BALP). If the HCERT is not verified, there is no digital verification: the verifiable health link (VHL) is not followed and the records are treated like paper records. As in J3, loading the DID documents is a PRECONDITION of this visit, not a step in it: the hospital verifies against its cached copy of the trust list and needs no connection to do so. It refreshes this copy nightly or hourly, whereas an offline site such as the J3 clinic refreshes it roughly weekly.
